analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md, with no executable code in the supplied evidence. Two doc changes are visible: (1) lines 444-448 describe a graceful drain completing without coordinator acknowledgement only when no work is left and the provider has no registered coordinator session (the CLI then prints `not needed (no coordinator connection)`). A registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. (2) The patch adds a runtime-constants row for a 30 s coordinator handshake deadline in CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift; that row falls in the truncated part of the excerpt and is not visible in the numbered units. This is relevant to TB-002 availability and to the provider-lifecycle drain semantics. The documented behaviour does not weaken a visible control. Drain-without-ack applies only with zero accepted work and no registered session, so there is no in-flight response to lose, and the coordinator protocol barrier text at lines 452-453 is unchanged. The logout, token-revocation, App Attest, prefix-cache and add-on hold text in the numbered units is unchanged context (T-041, T-053, TB-012), with no changed-line evidence of a regression. Unverified: the actual implementation in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift / ServiceDrain.swift, and whether a 'no registered session' state could be spoofed or produced by a coordinator-side disconnect to make a stop or restart skip acknowledgement while work is still being accepted. That is a code-level question outside this docs-only change. I identified no concrete security regression. Deeper review is not required for this documentation change, but integration should confirm the code matches the stated conditions if the source is in scope.
